clue.text: Assigned soldiers, exhausted, to abandon river

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped from the word before

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
drained means worn out
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Troops, worn out, are posted elsewhere and must leave the river behind.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordained can mean decreed or appointed, so something ordained has been formally allotted.

clue.text: Unconvincing fellow ditched by lover

indicators.note: something ditched is thrown away, so this letter is removed from the following word

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
an old flame is a former lover

explanation.surface: A weak-willed man is dumped by his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAME without its F leaves LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame excuse is a feeble one that fails to persuade anybody.

clue.text: Sexy lady lit up about revolutionary gear

indicators.note: up here means stirred up or in turmoil, so the letters are disordered
a revolution turns something round, so the word for gear is read backwards
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the turned word

blocks.note: taken as written
rig is equipment or kit

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman, tipsy, wearing some outrageous outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' reads as drunk, but 'up' is the anagram signal; the turned gear sits between the first two letters and the last.
explanation.definitionFit: An it girl is a glamorous young woman with sex appeal, 'it' once being slang for allure.

clue.text: Driven wild after young adult broached source of booze

indicators.note: wild suggests out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
broached means pierced, so the shuffled letters are opened up to admit the abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
YA is the publishing abbreviation for young adult

explanation.surface: Someone driven to madness after a teenager has opened the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A vineyard grows the grapes that become wine, so it is where the drink originates.

clue.text: Hint on poem given in articles from far away

indicators.note: given in means placed inside, so the pair goes within the two articles

blocks.note: AN is the indefinite article; two of them form the outside
a tip is a helpful hint
an ode is a lyric poem
the second indefinite article closes the word

explanation.surface: A tip about a poem tucked into some newspaper pieces sent from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' supplies two ANs, one each side of TIP ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes Australia and New Zealand, lands on the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: American sausage to go with German one picked up

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted upwards, so the German word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: to go, informally, is to urinate, which is to wee
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: An American hot dog to accompany a German one being collected.
explanation.walkthrough: WEE is the British childish word for urinating; EIN reversed gives NIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weenie is a US colloquial name for a frankfurter or wiener.

clue.text: Mother’s heading in to make a meal

indicators.note: a heading is what stands at the top, so only the word's opening letter is wanted
in means placed inside, so the single letter goes within the verb

blocks.note: to create is to make
the first letter of Mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum is going in to cook some food.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon meal of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream, a West Country tradition.

clue.text: Grand university in Australia, displaying learning?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the two letters are set within the country's abbreviation

blocks.note: Aust is the abbreviation for Australia
G is short for grand, a thousand
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A grand Australian university showing off its scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like the definition, and august does mean grand, but here it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: August means venerable and dignified, the air of a revered scholar; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Cans not opening with buttons?

indicators.note: with no opening, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: tinnies is slang for cans of beer

explanation.surface: Tins that won't open, and come with buttons attached.
explanation.walkthrough: TINNIES (cans of beer in British and Australian slang) without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Innies are navels that sink inwards; belly buttons, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Trick Judge with copy

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: Fooling a judge by using a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank played on someone.

clue.text: Mistakenly tenderising steak initially not required as part of recipe

indicators.note: done mistakenly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order
initially means at the start, so only the leading letter is taken
what is not required is left out, so that letter is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of steak

explanation.surface: A cook wrongly tenderising meat that the recipe never asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one S from TENDERISING, then rearrange the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Each food item a cook combines to make a dish is called an ingredient; the clue simply describes it.

clue.text: Coat, Picasso’s article, in which celebrity appears

indicators.note: in which tells us the second thing sits inside the first

blocks.note: el is 'the' in Picasso's native Spanish
a big name is a famous person

explanation.surface: A jacket, the subject of a piece on Picasso, featuring a famous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy layer of paint or glaze applied as a covering.

clue.text: Main area out at sea, nothing less? That’s where you’d have seen me!

definitions.text: That’s where you’d have seen me!

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder
less means minus, so the letter for zero is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An ocean voice boasting it was out on the main, at sea, no less.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one O from MAIN AREA OUT and rearrange. The Mauretania was a famous Cunard ocean liner launched in 1906, so the 'me' speaking is the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The liner Mauretania carried passengers across the Atlantic, so a traveller would have spotted her on the open sea.

clue.text: Don’t go and suspend deliveries

blocks.note: to stay an order is to suspend it
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler

explanation.surface: A plea to remain, and to halt the post or milk round.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is a bat-and-ball sport; an over is six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay over is to remain somewhere overnight rather than leaving.

clue.text: Dickens’s foremost eponymous character is a downtrodden worker

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of Dickens
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Claims that a Dickens title hero is a put-upon labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eponymous' points to a character who gives his name to the book, here Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge is someone who does menial, tedious work for others with little reward.

clue.text: Wearing certain hosiery as variety of diet gear

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are offered in another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in particular legwear as a form of slimming kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiters are coverings for the lower leg and ankle, so someone gaitered has them on.

clue.text: Part of speech: sailor taking in Democrat version

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the sailor surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
ver is an abbreviation for version

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: a seaman adopting a Democratic account.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is one of the word classes of grammar, modifying verbs and adjectives.

clue.text: Couple departed having removed fine jewellery item

indicators.note: having removed means having taken out, so a letter goes from the word for departed

blocks.note: a brace is a pair
left means went away
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A couple left after removing a fine piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine jewellery' reads as one phrase, but 'fine' is the F that comes out of LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band or chain worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Period of fasting: hour covers good duration

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so the earlier pair wraps around the letter for good

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
G is the abbreviation for good
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A Lenten fast where each hour stretches into a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: LENT followed by H covers G, which slips in before the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Length can mean the extent of time something lasts, as in the length of a film.

clue.text: Crazy Americans missing first fish in place for angling?

indicators.note: missing the first letter means the opening letter is cut off

blocks.note: in US slang a flake is an eccentric or crazy person
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Mad Americans who forgot the first fish, in a fishing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' looks like an anagram signal, but 'Crazy Americans' is US slang flakes, minus its F.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore of a lake is a natural place to fish; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Getting on? Getting on, even after soldiers are withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn troops are pulled out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: people getting on are agreeing with each other
RE stands for Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Is friendship still holding, even once the army has pulled out?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is used twice: once for growing old, once for agreeing, which loses RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, which is what ageing means.

clue.text: Superior person backing classy, but unusual form of gardening

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for the superior person is read right to left

blocks.note: a snob acts superior to others
A1 means first-class; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A snooty type supporting something stylish yet odd in horticulture.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots, a distinctive kind of cultivation.

clue.text: Indication of rebound protecting European aerospace company

indicators.note: protecting means shielding all round, so the sound effect encloses the letter

blocks.note: boing is the noise of something bouncing
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A sign of recovery shielding a European plane maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebound' suggests reversal, but here it is the bounce whose cartoon sound is BOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Boeing is the American manufacturer of airliners and spacecraft.

clue.text: Cricket side allege fiddling bringing in a top lawyer

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters are messed about
bringing in means admitting something inside before the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket team claims cheating and hires a first-rate barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal eagle is an informal idiom for a sharp, highly capable lawyer.

clue.text: Look for overturned fortresses that have yielded power

indicators.note: overturned means turned the other way, so the word is read backwards
having yielded means having given up, so a letter is surrendered

blocks.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Searching for toppled castles that have surrendered their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to search for or try to find.

clue.text: Where you’ll find some Scots broadcaster superior to English

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A broadcaster thought better than the English one, found among Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, superior means placed above, so SKY sits over E.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast, home to a Scottish population.

clue.text: Concealed passport possibly caught in part of wash cycle, losing front

indicators.note: caught means trapped, so the document ends up held within the other word
losing its front means the leading letter is dropped

blocks.note: the rinse is one stage of a washing-machine programme
a passport is one form of identification

explanation.surface: A hidden passport got stuck in the washing machine and ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: RINSE loses its R to leave INSE, which holds ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inside is enclosed within and so hidden from view.

clue.text: Single unknown item to exist in grasp of that male worker?

indicators.note: in the grasp of means held inside, so the run of pieces sits within the pronoun

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a male
one is a single unit
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A single mystery object held by some man, a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' is a link word here. The male in the clue is a red herring: worker bees are female.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker is the name for the sterile female bees that gather nectar for the hive.
